# Implementing Domain-Driven Design plugin: component map

This file is the plan the components were built from. It lists every component with its purpose, the upstream sections it applies, and the one-sentence reason it is not a duplicate of its nearest sibling.
Upstream sections are the `##` headings of `skills/principles/references/full.md` (19 sections, a short rule set). A few `###` headings are cited where only a slice of a section applies.

## Design decisions

1. **The rule set is short, so components are separated by role and by situation, not by rewording.** The same aggregate rule appears as a rules skill (`ddd-implementing-aggregate-boundaries`), a manual workflow that produces evidence (`ddd-implementing-invariant-inventory`), a reviewer that reports a ledger (`ddd-implementing-aggregate-design-reviewer`) and an implementer that changes code (`ddd-implementing-identity-reference-converter`). Each of the four has a different trigger, output and permission set. No component restates another cluster's rules; it points to the sibling.
2. **Implementation depth, not discovery.** The sibling plugins `ddd` and `ddd-distilled` own model discovery, strategic classification and low-ceremony adoption. This plugin owns what happens in code once DDD is chosen: where an aggregate ends, how outsiders reach it, how two aggregates coordinate, what a repository looks like, how a domain event is named and carried, how an application service stays thin, how a foreign model is translated, what a client sees. Subdomain classification and event storming are not reproduced here.
3. **The brake is a first-class cluster.** The source repeats that DDD vocabulary without design change and over-modeling trivial CRUD are both failures. `ddd-implementing-core-domain-focus` (rules), `ddd-implementing-ceremony-check` (keep, trim or extract plan per named area) and `ddd-implementing-modeling-effort-reviewer` (review of the changed code in a diff) carry it, so the tactical skills can assume the work is justified. The same trio also guards against the opposite failure, refusing to model real complexity.
4. **The aggregate rules are split along the four sub-sections of the source, merged where the code situation is the same.** Boundaries (what is inside), root discipline (how outsiders touch it) and cross-aggregate coordination (identity references plus one-aggregate-per-transaction) are three skills because a reader meets them as three different questions in code: "what belongs here", "who may call this", "why does this use case save two things".
5. **Integration is split by direction.** `ddd-implementing-context-mapping` decides the relationship, `ddd-implementing-anticorruption-layer` builds the inbound translation, `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` shapes what leaves the context, `ddd-implementing-client-representations` shapes what a UI or API client sees. A fifth concern, ownership of code inside one context, is `ddd-implementing-bounded-context` plus `ddd-implementing-module-structure`.
6. **Testing Rules get their own skill, reviewer and implementer.** The source has seven testing rules covering seven different layers; `ddd-implementing-domain-tests` states them, `ddd-implementing-test-coverage-reviewer` maps changed behavior to tests, `ddd-implementing-domain-test-writer` writes them.
7. **Model-invocable skills are capped at 20.** There are 20. Everything that is a procedure with arguments is manual.
8. **Reviewers own one concern and have their own output shape.** The context-boundary reviewer reports an ownership table, the translation reviewer a crossing inventory, the language reviewer a term ledger, the aggregate-design reviewer an aggregate ledger, the root-discipline reviewer an access-path table, the transaction reviewer a transaction map, the repository reviewer a contract table, the event reviewer an event catalog, the rule-placement reviewer a decision ledger, the representation reviewer an exposure table, the modeling-effort reviewer severity-ranked findings plus the areas the change touched, the test-coverage reviewer a test matrix.
9. **Provenance is labeled.** Rules written as `[MUST]`, `[MUST NOT]`, `[MUST NOT by default]`, `[SHOULD]`, `[SHOULD NOT]` or `[MAY]` come from `full.md` and keep its modal strength (an unqualified rule is MUST, `Prefer`/`should usually`/`unless there is a compelling reason` is SHOULD, `Do not`/`MUST NOT` is MUST NOT, `Do not ... by default` is MUST NOT by default, `Avoid by default` is SHOULD NOT). Rules that exist only in the compact files are marked `[Compact checklist]` and the plugin's own heuristics, detection recipes and numeric search aids are marked `[Added judgment]`.
10. **The lead is lean.** It names at most five steps and proposes implementers only when changes were requested.

## Confusable pairs

Model-invocable skills whose descriptions could fire on the same request, and the clause that separates them. The separating clause is written into the description of at least one skill of every pair, and into both where the 300-character budget allows.

Two situations produce the most overlap, so the descriptions are written around the question each skill answers rather than around the code symptom:

- **A shared class, enum, table or package serving several contexts.** `ddd-implementing-bounded-context` is triggered by "who owns this and may it be shared at all" (class, enum or model, never folders), `ddd-implementing-module-structure` by "where does the folder or package go" (a tree, a `shared` or `common` package), and `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` by "what leaves the context" (a message, payload, identifier or table access). Its description no longer names shared enums or packages; those rules stay in its body and are reached through the sibling pointers.
- **A service that reads state, branches and writes it back.** `ddd-implementing-aggregate-root-discipline` is triggered by the access surface (setters, exposed child collections, navigation through internals) and says that where the deciding code lives belongs to a sibling; `ddd-implementing-application-services` by a use-case method whose branching keeps growing; `ddd-implementing-domain-services` by a domain-layer operation that needs several objects and fits none, or a domain-named mapper; `ddd-implementing-core-domain-focus` by an area-level question (flat records and scripts over real lifecycle, or CRUD wrapped in aggregates) and no longer names service branching.

| Pair | Separating clause |
| --- | --- |
| `ddd-implementing-aggregate-boundaries` / `ddd-implementing-aggregate-root-discipline` | What belongs inside one aggregate and how big it is, versus how code outside the aggregate is allowed to reach and change it. |
| `ddd-implementing-aggregate-boundaries` / `ddd-implementing-cross-aggregate-coordination` | The inside of one aggregate, versus the relationship between two (references, transactions, eventual consistency). |
| `ddd-implementing-aggregate-root-discipline` / `entities` | Access path and mutation rights from outside, versus identity, lifecycle and transition rules of one entity. |
| `entities` / `ddd-implementing-value-objects` | Has identity and a lifecycle, versus is defined by its attributes and is immutable. |
| `ddd-implementing-domain-services` / `ddd-implementing-application-services` | A domain-layer decision that spans several domain objects, versus use-case orchestration (load, call, save, publish) and the branching that creeps into it. |
| `ddd-implementing-aggregate-root-discipline` / `ddd-implementing-application-services` | The access surface an outsider can use (setters, exposed children, getter-then-decide), versus the shape of the use-case method that does the calling (orchestration, not rules). A service that reads state, branches and writes back is both; the first reports the reachable internals, the second where the rules should sit. |
| `ddd-implementing-aggregate-root-discipline` / `ddd-implementing-domain-services` | Reachable internals of one aggregate, versus an operation that needs several objects and fits none of them. |
| `ddd-implementing-core-domain-focus` / `ddd-implementing-domain-services` | Whether an area earns a model at all, versus how to build one domain-layer operation that fits no single object in an area that is already modeled. |
| `ddd-implementing-domain-events` / `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` | A fact inside the model (name, payload, when to raise), versus a message that leaves the context (contract model, identifiers). |
| `ddd-implementing-domain-events` / `ddd-implementing-event-sourcing` | Events as announced facts, versus events as the persistence model of an aggregate. |
| `ddd-implementing-anticorruption-layer` / `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` | Foreign model coming in, versus local model going out. |
| `ddd-implementing-context-mapping` / `ddd-implementing-anticorruption-layer` | Choosing and recording the relationship and who translates, versus building the translator. |
| `ddd-implementing-context-mapping` / `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` | Deciding the relationship, influence and who translates between two contexts, versus shaping the outgoing message or identifier that crosses. |
| `ddd-implementing-bounded-context` / `ddd-implementing-module-structure` | Which context owns a concept and whether one class or enum may be shared at all, versus folder and package layout. For a `shared` or `common` package the first decides whether the class may exist once, the second where the folders go. |
| `ddd-implementing-bounded-context` / `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` | Who owns a concept and whether one class or enum serves several contexts, versus the shape of the message, identifier or table access that leaves a context. |
| `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` / `ddd-implementing-module-structure` | What crosses between contexts, versus where a `shared` or `common` package and the other folders sit in the tree. |
| `ddd-implementing-bounded-context` / `ddd-implementing-ubiquitous-language` | Where a model is valid, versus which word names a concept inside one context. |
| `ddd-implementing-client-representations` / `repositories` | What a UI or API client receives and how read models are shaped, versus how an aggregate is stored and reconstituted. |
| `ddd-implementing-client-representations` / `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` | Clients of this application, versus other bounded contexts. |
| `ddd-implementing-core-domain-focus` / `ddd-implementing-application-services` | Whether a supporting area may stay simple CRUD, versus how thin an application service is in an area that is modeled. |
| `repositories` / `ddd-implementing-application-services` | The persistence contract for an aggregate root, versus the use-case code that calls it. |

## Skills: model-invocable (20)

| Name | Purpose | Upstream sections | Distinct from its nearest sibling because |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `principles` | Hub: bias, loading order, modal convention and tags, routing table to every component, priorities, final checklist | Purpose; Primary Directive; Code Generation Rules; Review Checklist; Final Instruction | It decides which other component to use; it holds no cluster rules itself. |
| `ddd-implementing-bounded-context` | Name the context before interpreting anything, validity of a model inside one context, no global model, no shared domain package, boundary in code | Strategic Design Rules; Bounded Context Is Mandatory; Primary Directive | `ddd-implementing-module-structure` lays out folders; this decides which context owns a concept and whether a model is being shared. |
| `ddd-implementing-context-mapping` | Explicit relationship per interaction, translation responsibility, upstream/downstream influence, the map as a design artifact kept beside the code | Strategic Design Rules; Context Mapping Is a Design Artifact; Context Integration Rules | `ddd-implementing-anticorruption-layer` builds the translator; this decides that one is needed, who owns it, and who has influence over whom. |
| `ddd-implementing-anticorruption-layer` | Translate a foreign or legacy model into local language, keep foreign schemas and statuses out, own and test the translation | Context Integration Rules; Anticorruption Layer; Domain and Transformation Service Rules; Testing Rules | Inbound only; `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` is the outbound mirror. |
| `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` | Identifiers and integration messages across contexts, contract models separate from local models, no shared enums, no database coupling, composition above the models | Context Integration Rules; Identity Across Contexts; Client Representation and Scope Discipline | Outbound only; `ddd-implementing-domain-events` is the in-model fact, this is the shape that leaves. |
| `ddd-implementing-ubiquitous-language` | One term per concept, one concept per term, local names in classes, methods, events, tests and packages, rename on understanding | Ubiquitous Language Rules; Review Rules | `ddd-implementing-bounded-context` says where a model is valid; this says which word names what inside it. |
| `ddd-implementing-core-domain-focus` | Spend modeling effort where complexity lives, protect the core from generic and vendor terms, keep supporting areas simple, refuse DDD theater and refuse under-modeling | Strategic Design Rules; Core Domain Protection; Practical Simplicity Rule; Primary Directive | It decides whether tactical machinery is earned; every other tactical skill assumes it is. |
| `ddd-implementing-aggregate-boundaries` | Boundaries from immediate invariants, smallest aggregate, no ORM-shaped aggregates, conservative boundary, invariants on the root | Aggregate Rules of Thumb; Aggregates Are Consistency Boundaries; Code Generation Rules | `ddd-implementing-cross-aggregate-coordination` is about the link between aggregates; this is about the inside of one. |
| `ddd-implementing-aggregate-root-discipline` | Only the root is referenced from outside, invariant changes go through the root, no setters, no exposed mutable children, no read-decide-write outside | Aggregate Rules of Thumb; Aggregate Root Discipline; Review Rules | `entities` covers one entity's behavior; this covers who is allowed to reach the aggregate's insides. |
| `ddd-implementing-cross-aggregate-coordination` | Identity references, no graph loading, one aggregate per transaction by default, events/policies/process coordination, proof before a multi-aggregate transaction | Aggregate Rules of Thumb; Reference Other Aggregates by Identity; One Aggregate per Transaction by Default; Final Instruction | `ddd-implementing-aggregate-boundaries` sizes one aggregate; this governs how two interact. |
| `entities` | Identity and lifecycle, protected state transitions, behavior not generic state change, no passive ORM container | Entity and Value Object Rules; Entities; Testing Rules | `ddd-implementing-value-objects` is identity-less; `ddd-implementing-aggregate-root-discipline` is about outsiders. |
| `ddd-implementing-value-objects` | Immutable by default, validation at construction, value equality, replace meaningful primitives, enforcement near the concept | Entity and Value Object Rules; Value Objects; Testing Rules | `entities` is identity; this is attribute-defined meaning. |
| `ddd-implementing-domain-services` | A domain service only for a domain operation that fits no entity or value object, domain naming, transformation services, technical mapping outside | Domain and Transformation Service Rules | `ddd-implementing-application-services` orchestrates use cases; this holds a domain decision. |
| `repositories` | One per aggregate root, domain-defined interface, reconstitute and persist, no generic CRUD, no rows, no rules inside | Repository Rules; Testing Rules | `ddd-implementing-client-representations` shapes reads for clients; this is the aggregate's persistence contract. |
| `ddd-implementing-domain-events` | Meaningful facts, past tense, part of the model, local payload, no property-change events, no commands in disguise, raised by behavior | Domain Event Rules; Application Service Rules; Testing Rules | `ddd-implementing-event-sourcing` is a persistence choice; `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` is the message leaving the context. |
| `ddd-implementing-event-sourcing` | Only when the event sequence is the right persistence model, stream and version tied to aggregate identity, deterministic replay, event versioning | Domain Event Rules; Event Sourcing | It decides storage by events; `ddd-implementing-domain-events` governs events as facts either way. |
| `ddd-implementing-application-services` | Use-case coordination, load/invoke/persist/publish, transaction ownership, no core decisions, controllers do not duplicate orchestration | Application Service Rules; Code Generation Rules; Testing Rules | `ddd-implementing-domain-services` owns domain decisions; this refuses to. |
| `ddd-implementing-module-structure` | Contexts first, then domain/use-case ownership, no `shared`/`common` domain package, model visible in structure | Module and Package Rules; Strategic Design Rules | `ddd-implementing-bounded-context` is about ownership of concepts; this is about directories and packages. |
| `ddd-implementing-client-representations` | DTOs, projections, use-case queries, rendition adapters, mediators, REST resources, command/query separation when justified, explicit scope identifiers | Client Representation and Scope Discipline | `ddd-implementing-integration-contracts` is for other contexts; this is for clients of this application. |
| `ddd-implementing-domain-tests` | Test aggregate invariants, transitions, value objects, events as outcomes, repositories as infrastructure, translation layers, application-service orchestration | Testing Rules; Ubiquitous Language Rules | It says what a test of each layer asserts; `ddd-implementing-test-coverage-reviewer` checks that they exist. |

| `plan` | no | no | Plan a change to existing code: edit order, tests first, hand-offs, stop conditions | Code Generation Rules; Testing Rules; Final Instruction | `ddd-implementing-model-walk` decides the shape of a new concept; `plan` sequences the edits. |

| `fix` | no | yes | Resolve named findings with the smallest change, run tests, never commit | Review Rules; Code Generation Rules; Review Checklist | The implementers each own one finding family; `fix` resolves a mixed list in the session. |
| `ddd-implementing-model-walk` | no | no | Walk a new concept through the nine code-generation steps and produce a model sheet before any code | Code Generation Rules; Primary Directive | `plan` sequences edits to existing code; this produces the design decisions a plan then uses. |
| `ddd-implementing-invariant-inventory` | no | no | List the invariants of an aggregate or use case, decide which must hold immediately, and propose or defend a boundary | Aggregate Rules of Thumb; Code Generation Rules | `ddd-implementing-aggregate-boundaries` states the rules; this produces the evidence the rules demand when a boundary changes or a transaction spans aggregates. |
| `ddd-implementing-context-map` | yes | no | Reconstruct the context map as found: contexts, relationships, translation points, leaks | Strategic Design Rules; Context Integration Rules | `ddd-implementing-context-boundary-reviewer` and `ddd-implementing-translation-reviewer` judge a diff; this scans a tree. |
| `ddd-implementing-ceremony-check` | no | no | Plan, for named areas, what to keep, trim or extract so the modeling matches the complexity, with evidence per signal | Practical Simplicity Rule; Strategic Design Rules | `ddd-implementing-core-domain-focus` is the rule set and `ddd-implementing-modeling-effort-reviewer` judges only the changed code of a diff; this reads whole named areas and produces an ordered plan for the team. |

## Subagents (21)

Reviewers are read-only (`Read, Grep, Glob, Bash`, `Write` and `Edit` disallowed). Implementers also have `Edit` and `Write`.

| Name | Model | Purpose | Skills preloaded | Upstream sections | Distinct from its nearest sibling because |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ddd-implementing-lead` | opus | Routes a task or diff to at most five steps; does not review | principles | Primary Directive; Review Rules | Only agent that does not read code for defects. |
| `ddd-implementing-final-gate` | sonnet | Runs the ten checklist questions plus five compact additions on the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL | principles | Review Checklist; Final Instruction | Binary gate with evidence; reviewers return ranked findings. |
| `ddd-implementing-context-boundary-reviewer` | sonnet | Ownership of code by context, shared domain packages, global models, boundary only in diagrams, package layout | bounded-context, module-structure | Strategic Design Rules; Module and Package Rules; Review Rules | Output is an ownership table; `ddd-implementing-translation-reviewer` inventories crossings. |
| `ddd-implementing-translation-reviewer` | sonnet | Every place a model crosses a context or system boundary: direction, type, where translated | anticorruption-layer, integration-contracts | Context Integration Rules; Domain and Transformation Service Rules | Output is a crossing inventory; it never judges placement of code in packages. |
| `ddd-implementing-language-reviewer` | sonnet | Synonyms, homonyms, technical placeholders in classes, methods, events, tests, packages | ubiquitous-language | Ubiquitous Language Rules | Output is a term ledger per context. |
| `ddd-implementing-aggregate-design-reviewer` | sonnet | Aggregate size, invariants that justify each member, object references to other aggregates | aggregate-boundaries, cross-aggregate-coordination | Aggregate Rules of Thumb | Looks at model classes; `ddd-implementing-transaction-reviewer` looks at use cases. |
| `ddd-implementing-root-discipline-reviewer` | sonnet | Ways outside code can reach and change aggregate internals | aggregate-root-discipline, entities | Aggregate Rules of Thumb; Entity and Value Object Rules | Output is an access-path table; `ddd-implementing-rule-placement-reviewer` owns where branching decisions live. |
| `ddd-implementing-transaction-reviewer` | sonnet | Aggregates modified per transaction and the invariant that justifies each | cross-aggregate-coordination, application-services | Aggregate Rules of Thumb; Application Service Rules | Output is a transaction map. |
| `ddd-implementing-value-object-reviewer` | sonnet | Primitives that hide meaning, mutable or unvalidated value types, identity-compared values | value-objects | Entity and Value Object Rules | Output is a primitive-and-value ledger. |
| `ddd-implementing-repository-reviewer` | sonnet | Repository shape, return types, business rules inside, one-per-root | repositories | Repository Rules | Output is a contract table. |
| `ddd-implementing-event-reviewer` | sonnet | Event names, fact versus command, payload, property-change events | domain-events | Domain Event Rules | Output is an event catalog; `ddd-implementing-event-sourcing-reviewer` checks streams. |
| `ddd-implementing-event-sourcing-reviewer` | sonnet | Whether event sourcing is justified; stream identity, versioning, replay determinism, upcasting | event-sourcing | Domain Event Rules | Output is a per-aggregate stream checklist; only relevant when events are persisted. |
| `ddd-implementing-rule-placement-reviewer` | sonnet | Where branching business decisions live: model, domain service, application service, controller, repository | application-services, domain-services | Application Service Rules; Domain and Transformation Service Rules | Output is a decision ledger; it is the only reviewer that traces a rule to its rightful owner. |
| `ddd-implementing-representation-reviewer` | sonnet | Aggregates, rows or foreign types exposed to clients; representation per client; scope identifiers | client-representations | Client Representation and Scope Discipline | Output is an exposure table. |
| `ddd-implementing-modeling-effort-reviewer` | sonnet | Over-modeled CRUD, under-modeled complexity, DDD vocabulary without design change, in the changed code of a diff | core-domain-focus | Practical Simplicity Rule; Strategic Design Rules | Output is severity-ranked findings with `file:line` plus an areas list; the only reviewer that argues for less structure. `ddd-implementing-ceremony-check` plans whole areas. |
| `ddd-implementing-test-coverage-reviewer` | sonnet | Changed domain behavior mapped to the layer of test the rules call for | domain-tests | Testing Rules | Output is a test matrix; `ddd-implementing-domain-test-writer` writes tests, this finds gaps. |
| `ddd-implementing-root-encapsulator` | sonnet | Moves invariant-changing logic behind aggregate root methods, closes setters and exposed collections | aggregate-root-discipline, application-services | Aggregate Rules of Thumb; Application Service Rules | Moves existing logic into the model; `ddd-implementing-identity-reference-converter` changes references. |
| `ddd-implementing-identity-reference-converter` | sonnet | Replaces object references between aggregates with identities, and splits an oversized aggregate along them | cross-aggregate-coordination, aggregate-boundaries | Aggregate Rules of Thumb | Structural change of what a field holds; `ddd-implementing-transaction-splitter` changes use-case behavior. |
| `ddd-implementing-transaction-splitter` | sonnet | Splits a multi-aggregate transaction into one transaction per aggregate coordinated by a domain event | cross-aggregate-coordination, domain-events | Aggregate Rules of Thumb; Domain Event Rules | Changes consistency timing, so it requires an invariant inventory first. |
| `ddd-implementing-acl-builder` | sonnet | Builds a translator and a narrow port in local language around a foreign or legacy model | anticorruption-layer | Context Integration Rules | Edits the boundary only; reviews nothing. |
| `ddd-implementing-domain-test-writer` | sonnet | Writes tests for invariants, transitions, value objects, events and translators in the ubiquitous language | domain-tests | Testing Rules | Writes tests only; never edits production code. |

## Output styles (6)

| Name | Observable behavior | Upstream sections | Distinct because |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mentor` | Names the rule and its strength behind each choice, ends non-trivial answers with one check question | Purpose; Final Instruction | Teaching is the only goal. |
| `strict-reviewer` | Output is a ranked findings table, no rewrites unless asked, explicit "No findings" | Review Rules; Review Checklist | Never changes code. |
| `pair` | Small steps, narrates intent, asks before changing an aggregate boundary, a public contract or anything past a few lines | Code Generation Rules; Aggregate Rules of Thumb | Interaction rhythm. |
| `terse` | Result first, a few lines, failing output still in full | Final Instruction | Brevity rules. |
| `context-first` | Every design or code answer opens with the bounded context, the local terms and the relationship to neighbors; asks one question when the context is unknown | Primary Directive; Strategic Design Rules; Ubiquitous Language Rules | Strategic frame precedes every answer. |
| `invariant-first` | Before any change to an aggregate, transaction or event, prints the invariants, the boundary decision and the transaction scope, then the change | Aggregate Rules of Thumb; Domain Event Rules | Tactical frame precedes every change. |

## Overlap review

Pairs that were close and how they were separated:

- The four aggregate skills (`ddd-implementing-aggregate-boundaries`, `ddd-implementing-aggregate-root-discipline`, `ddd-implementing-cross-aggregate-coordination`, `entities`) never restate each other: size and membership, outside access, links between aggregates, one entity's lifecycle. The anti-pattern list in the source is distributed, one owner each: ORM-shaped aggregates to `ddd-implementing-aggregate-boundaries`, exposed mutable child collections to `ddd-implementing-aggregate-root-discipline`, transactions updating many aggregates and cross-aggregate navigation to `ddd-implementing-cross-aggregate-coordination`.
- `ddd-implementing-domain-events` and `ddd-implementing-event-sourcing` share the anti-patterns about events carrying persistence artifacts; the owner is `ddd-implementing-domain-events`, and `ddd-implementing-event-sourcing` points to it.
- `ddd-implementing-root-discipline-reviewer` and `ddd-implementing-rule-placement-reviewer` can both see "a service reads state, branches and writes it back". The first reports the reachable internals (the access path), the second reports where the branching rule lives and who should own it. Each names the other instead of repeating the finding.
- `ddd-implementing-aggregate-design-reviewer` and `ddd-implementing-transaction-reviewer` both mention cross-aggregate coordination. The first reads model classes for references and size, the second reads use cases for the aggregates saved per transaction.
- `ddd-implementing-translation-reviewer` and `ddd-implementing-context-boundary-reviewer`: ownership of code (a package, a shared domain package, a global model) versus crossings (an import across contexts, a foreign status in a local type, a shared enum). Imports between contexts are always the translation reviewer's.
- `ddd-implementing-ceremony-check` and `ddd-implementing-modeling-effort-reviewer` share the three signals, which live only in `ddd-implementing-core-domain-focus` rule 10 (the skill keeps a three-bullet gloss, the agent only points to the rule). They differ by situation and output: `ddd-implementing-ceremony-check` takes named areas, reads them whole and prints a keep, trim or extract plan with an ordered list of steps for the team; the reviewer judges only what a diff adds or changes and prints findings by severity with `file:line`, naming `ddd-implementing-ceremony-check` when the untouched rest of an area looks wrong.
- `ddd-implementing-modeling-effort-reviewer` and `ddd-implementing-application-services`/`ddd-implementing-rule-placement-reviewer`: the effort reviewer argues about how much structure an area earns; the placement reviewer assumes the area is modeled and checks where decisions live.
- `plan`, `ddd-implementing-model-walk` and `ddd-implementing-lead`: `ddd-implementing-lead` routes components, `ddd-implementing-model-walk` decides the shape of a new concept, `plan` orders the edits of an existing codebase. `plan` sends new concepts to `ddd-implementing-model-walk` rather than redoing it.
- `review`, `audit`, `checklist`, `ddd-implementing-final-gate`: judge a change; rate a tree; walk the checklist interactively; return PASS or FAIL in isolation.

The source has no section on factories, domain-event delivery mechanics, process managers or CQRS infrastructure beyond the single rule on separating command behavior from query models. This plugin does not invent them: where a heuristic goes beyond the rule set (idempotent handlers, outbox, snapshots, stream versions) it is labeled `[Added judgment]`.
